title: Myth vs Reality: was Napoleon short?

segments.text: Reality: he was about average for his time.
Records say he measured five feet two inches.
But that was in French units, and the French inch was longer than the English one.
Converted, he stood about five foot six or seven, a little above the typical Frenchman of his day.
So where did the myth come from?
British cartoonists, like James Gillray, drew him as Little Boney, a tantrum-throwing child.
His own soldiers called him the little corporal, as a term of affection.
And he was often surrounded by tall Imperial Guards, which made him look small.
The cartoons lasted longer than the facts.

verify: Recorded 5'2" in French units (~1.686 m); 'a little above typical Frenchman' (avg ~1.64 m)
